title: The motion-model bank becomes the threat
summary: An IMM tuned for ±6 degree-per-second turns loses both when the target stays straight and when it turns beyond the bank at 12 degrees per second.
trigger: Hold the three-mode bank fixed and sweep the true turn rate through 0, 3, 6, and 12 degrees per second.
observed: At 0 degrees per second the IMM OSPA rises from 21.59 to 31.42; at 12 degrees per second it rises from 42.41 to 49.33.
invariant: A model bank must be sized against the expected threat set and compared with its single-model baseline across the full regime.
fix: Report the operating band, retain the sweep, and resize the modes only with an explicit trade against straight-motion cost.

timeline.title: Leave the designed band
timeline.detail: The target either never turns or doubles the strongest turn rate represented in the bank.

timeline.title: Misallocate model probability
timeline.detail: Unused noisy modes tax the straight case; unmatched dynamics tax the fast-turn case.

timeline.title: Sweep instead of cherry-pick
timeline.detail: Four paired regimes expose both ends where the headline model loses.

timeline.title: Publish the operating band
timeline.detail: The evidence claims benefit only in the measured 3–6 degree-per-second band.

limits: This is a specific three-model IMM bank, not a general claim that IMM fails outside ±6 degrees per second.
